title: Cyber Incident Command
tagline: Contain, brief, and escalate a live incident before the news cycle beats you to it.
painPoint: Cyber incidents get worse the longer it takes to get an accurate picture in front of the people who can authorize a response.

steps.caption: Incident command, live
steps.talk: This is cyber incident response the way it should work: the moment a threat is confirmed, the clock is already running against you.

steps.caption: Loading a real incident
steps.talk: We're loading a realistic incident — the kind that normally triggers an all-hands war room call and a scramble for a status update.

steps.caption: Six engines, one click
steps.talk: Six specialist engines — containment, forensics, compliance, comms, business impact, remediation — analyze this simultaneously. What normally takes a team an hour of frantic message threads happens here in seconds.

steps.caption: Escalate with full context
steps.talk: Escalating to the strategist — it doesn't start from zero, it inherits everything the engines already found.

steps.caption: Executive approval, one click
steps.talk: One click and this is now on the executive's desk with an approve action ready — no waiting on a 2am summary email.

steps.caption: The close
steps.talk: This is the pitch: response measured in seconds, not hours — and a fully documented decision trail for the board and regulators afterward.

cta: TSM compresses incident response from hours of Slack threads to a documented decision in minutes.
